analyst_view.overall: Frosinone (7th, 20 points) host Parma (17th, 8 points) after both lost 5-1 last weekend, Frosinone at Milan and Parma at home to Roma. Frosinone are short of centre-forwards: Raimondo is out until about January and Birligea went off hurt at San Siro, so Bobcek is expected to lead the line with Schmid behind him; the numbers now count both absences on goals (about -23% for Frosinone). Parma, under Alberto Gilardino, are without striker Romero (also counted on goals, -13%), while Drobnic and Diego Carlos trained apart this week and are at best on the bench; Diego Carlos is not in the numbers, and Ndiaye returns from his ban. Parma are fighting relegation and usually start cautiously in a 3-5-2 with Toure and Elphege up front. No referee has been named yet; since yesterday's view the numbers themselves dropped from 3.0 to 2.5 goals as they took in the strikers' absences, so my only move left is a small trim on shots, which the absences don't reach.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals (1.5 Frosinone, 1.0 Parma), down from 3.0 yesterday because they now take off Raimondo and Birligea for Frosinone and Romero for Parma, while still adding both teams' recent leaky defending (Frosinone conceded 13 in six games, Parma 12). Parma's back line is thinner than the numbers know, with Diego Carlos at best on the bench, but Frosinone's makeshift attack around Bobcek points the other way, so I stay at about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.5 corners, 7.5 of them Frosinone's, and already add +16% for Frosinone's 53 corners in their last six games. Parma are expected to sit back in a 3-5-2 for the first half hour as Gilardino usually does, which is the pattern the numbers already assume, so I stay at about 11.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards and already take a little off because both teams have been booked less than usual lately. Parma are in a relegation fight and Gilardino asked his side to be 'more ruthless', with Ndiaye back from a red-card ban, but no referee has been named and nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 38.2 shots, a very high figure built on +34% for Frosinone's 135 shots in their last six games. The striker absences are only taken off goals, not shots: Frosinone lose both Raimondo and Birligea and Bobcek is a different kind of forward, and Parma lose Romero, so I trim mildly to about 36.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.0 shots on target and already add +20% for Frosinone's recent accuracy. Without their two main centre-forwards Frosinone should test the goalkeeper a little less often, and Parma's attack without Romero is weak; a Parma defence missing Diego Carlos limits the trim, so I go to about 10.7.
